By the 20th century, it had spread to many more countries and even respectable media organisations had joined the capers. The BBC's “spaghetti harvest” segment in 1957 is thought to be the first April Fools prank pulled on TV.News broadcasters now walk a trickier tightrope, says Phoebe Hart (@qutrealworld), as audiences are fractured, suspicious and digitally-savvy. They're aware of entrenched inequality, scammers and bad actors, immoral leaders and elites, and corruptible institutions.
